week_in_brief: The ground just shifted beneath attribution models, retail-integrated care channels, and what patients believe about medicine.

items.headline: AI Citations Decoupled from Rankings. Your Visibility Strategy Needs Three Layers Now.
items.whats_happening: Google's May core update severed the link between page-one rankings and AI citations. Top-10 rankers dropped from 76% of AI citations in mid-2025 to 38% in early 2026. Google now prioritizes passage structure and information consistency across independent sources over backlink profiles. Meanwhile, Google eliminated tracking signals for AI Overview clicks in early May—meaning you can no longer identify which traffic came from AI answers, even as those answers suppress traditional click-through rates by 18–34% on B2B keywords.
items.so_what: You now need content strategies for three distinct visibility layers simultaneously—traditional rankings, AI citations, and agent-source-trust. Last-click models miss AI-influenced conversions entirely, creating an invisible attribution gap. Add self-reported attribution to intake forms and start tracking share of voice in AI responses as a primary KPI, not a secondary metric.

items.headline: Amazon Hires Amwell Founder. Retail-Integrated Care Models Are Now Your Patient Acquisition Competitor.
items.whats_happening: Amazon brought Dr. Roy Schoenberg—Amwell's co-founder—on as Senior VP of Health Services to lead Amazon Pharmacy, One Medical, and Health AI. Walmart integrated Teladoc into its Better Care Services platform, offering 24/7 virtual care, dermatology, nutrition, and prescription routing to any pharmacy. Both moves reflect retail-integrated care channels that capture patients at the point of shopping behavior, not health intent.
items.so_what: You're no longer competing only within your metro area against other hospitals. You're competing against care models embedded into consumer shopping behavior with zero geographic boundaries. If your acquisition strategy assumes patients start with a provider search, that assumption is breaking. Map where your target patients already spend time—and whether you have access to those channels.

items.headline: Meta Overtakes Google in Global Ad Revenue. Budget Allocation Built Around Google-First Needs Immediate Review.
items.whats_happening: Meta will generate $243.46 billion in global ad revenue in 2026, surpassing Google's $239.54 billion for the first time. Meta's growth accelerated to 24.1% year-over-year, driven by Reels momentum, Advantage+ AI automation, and WhatsApp expansion. Google's growth held at 11.9%, while AI Overviews and noisy search results consume top-of-page real estate without trackable attribution. ChatGPT also went self-serve with no minimum spend, processing 2.5 billion prompts daily and projecting $2.5B in 2026 revenue.
items.so_what: The default "Google gets 60% of our digital budget" model is now outdated. Meta's AI-powered automation is delivering measurable ROI faster than Google's increasingly complex search environment. Test ChatGPT for performance-oriented, high-intent offers\u201but understand it rewards specific intent matching, not brand awareness, and gives you zero user data. Revisit your budget allocation assumptions quarterly, not annually.

items.headline: Trust in Science and Medicine Is Eroding Among Patients. Credibility Is Now a Structural Marketing Problem.
items.whats_happening: The AMA CEO identified eroding trust in science, public health institutions, and medical professionals as a defining public health challenge—affecting vaccination rates, screening adoption, and help-seeking behavior. Patients increasingly turn to unproven treatments and misinformation sources. Separately, a JAMA Network Open study found long COVID affects approximately 1 in 6 COVID-positive adults\u201double the CDC's official estimate—yet physicians use the diagnostic code in less than 7% of cases, creating both clinical and marketing blind spots.
items.so_what: This isn't a communications task. It's a structural repositioning of how your system builds credibility with your community. Long COVID represents a measurable, underserved population your competitors are ignoring. Position your system as a leader in evidence-based diagnosis, patient registry, and specialized care pathways. Trust is now a competitive advantage, but only if it's backed by operational substance, not just messaging.

this_weeks_take: Most health systems still run marketing as if patients start with provider search, attribution is trackable, and competitors are local. All three assumptions broke in the last six months. The winners will be the ones who rethink acquisition channels, credibility positioning, and measurement infrastructure before the rest of the market catches up.
